content: 最近抓那种堆满图片和字体的动态页时，page.goto 的时间基本耗在无关资源上。想在 lib/index.js 的插件 options 里加两项配置：blockResourceTypes 数组，取值比如 image/font/media/stylesheet；以及 goto 用的 waitUntil 和 timeout。不传这些参数时行为和现在完全一致，老调用方不用改。 麻烦在别和 lib/requestRenderLock.js 互相踩：render lock 自己已经 setRequestInterception，还在 request 事件里维护 pending 计数，再挂一套监听各自调 continue/abort 的话，Puppeteer 会抛 Request is already handled。把资源类型判断并进现有的请求决策，同一个 request 只落一个结局，命中类型 abort、其余 continue；注意 abort 走的是 requestfailed 而不是 requestfinished，render lock 的计数释放得覆盖失败分支，不然 networkidle 类 waitUntil 会一直挂到超时。document 类型不能拦，否则导航直接白屏，入参里出现 document 或无法识别的类型名就抛清晰错误；waitUntil 限定 Puppeteer 合法值，timeout 为 0 时按不超时透传。 测试在 test/puppeteer-plugin.test.js 里补，用 file:// 加载 test/mock 下的页面，可能得新加一个引用本地 img 和 stylesheet 的 fixture：一组断言命中类型被 abort、其他请求正常 continue，一组把 timeout 调到极短、再延迟 document 放行来制造 TimeoutError，看 reject 是否干净抛出、pending 计数有没有残留。改完顺手跑 npm test，再 npx eslint lib test 看下风格。

content.content: 1 [![Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/website-scraper-puppeteer.svg?style=flat)](https://www.npmjs.org/package/website-scraper-puppeteer) 2 [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/website-scraper-puppeteer.svg?style=flat)](https://www.npmjs.org/package/website-scraper-puppeteer) 3 [![Node.js CI](https://github.com/website-scraper/website-scraper-puppeteer/actions/workflows/node.js.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/website-scraper/website-scraper-puppeteer) 4 [![Code Coverage](https://qlty.sh/gh/website-scraper/projects/website-scraper-puppeteer/coverage.svg)](https://qlty.sh/gh/website-scraper/projects/website-scraper-puppeteer) 5 6 # website-scraper-puppeteer 7 Plugin for [website-scraper](https://github.com/website-scraper/node-website-scraper) which returns html for dynamic websites using [puppeteer](https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer). 8 9 ## Sponsors 10 Maintenance of this project is made possible by all the [contributors](https://github.com/website-scraper/website-scraper-puppeteer/graphs/contributors) and [sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/s0ph1e). 11 If you'd like to sponsor this project and have your avatar or company logo appear below [click here](https://github.com/sponsors/s0ph1e). 💖 12 13 14 15 ## Requirements 16 * nodejs version >= 20 17 * website-scraper version >= 6 18 19 ## Installation 20 ```sh 21 npm install website-scraper website-scraper-puppeteer 22 ``` 23 24 ### Installing Chrome 25 26 Puppeteer normally downloads a compatible version of Chrome automatically during installation via a `postinstall` script. Starting with **npm v12**, lifecycle scripts (including `postinstall`) are disabled by default, so this automatic download no longer runs. You may then see an error like `Could not find Chrome (ver. ...)` when scraping. 27 28 If you use **npm v12 or newer** (or another package manager that blocks install scripts, e.g. recent `pnpm`), install Chrome manually after installing the packages: 29 30 ```sh 31 npx puppeteer browsers install chrome 32 ``` 33 34 Alternatives: 35 * Re-enable install scripts by adding `puppeteer` to the [`allowScripts`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#allow-scripts) field in your `package.json` (or `.npmrc`), so the browser is downloaded automatically again. 36 * Use a Chrome/Chromium already installed on your system by pointing Puppeteer to it via `launchOptions.executablePath` (or the `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` environment variable). 37 38 See Puppeteer's guide on [why automatic downloads can be blocked](https://pptr.dev/guides/installation#automatic-downloads-can-be-blocked) for more details. 39 40 ## Usage 41 ```javascript 42 import scrape from 'website-scraper'; 43 import PuppeteerPlugin from 'website-scraper-puppeteer'; 44 45 await scrape({ 46 urls: ['https://www.instagram.com/gopro/'], 47 directory: '/path/to/save', 48 plugins: [ 49 new PuppeteerPlugin({ 50 launchOptions: { headless: true }, /* optional */ 51 gotoOptions: { waitUntil: "networkidle0" }, /* optional */ 52 scrollToBottom: { timeout: 10000, viewportN: 10 }, /* optional */ 53 exclusiveRendering: true, /* optional */ 54 }) 55 ] 56 }); 57 ``` 58 Puppeteer plugin constructor accepts the following params: 59 * `launchOptions` - *(optional)* - puppeteer launch options, can be found in [puppeteer docs](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.launchoptions) 60 * `gotoOptions` - *(optional)* - puppeteer page.goto options, can be found in [puppeteer docs](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.gotooptions) 61 * `scrollToBottom` - *(optional)* - in some cases, the page needs to be scrolled down to render its assets (lazyloading). Because some pages can be really endless, the scrolldown process can be interrupted before reaching the bottom when one or both of the limitations below are reached: 62 * `timeout` - in milliseconds 63 * `viewportN` - viewport height multiplier 64 * `exclusiveRendering` - *(optional, default `true`)* - render pages one at a time and never while other requests are in flight, so cookies rotated by a page (see [Cookies](#cookies)) are never presented stale. Set to `false` for websites which don't rotate cookies: pages are then rendered concurrently, which is considerably faster on large websites. 65 66 ## Cookies 67 Cookies passed in `request.headers.Cookie` (website-scraper option) are set into the browser's cookie jar for the scraped urls' hosts (including their subdomains), so pages opened in puppeteer send them too — but they are not leaked to other domains. 68 This also applies when a scraped url redirects to a different host (e.g. `example.com` → `shop.example.net`): the redirect target does not receive the configured cookies unless its host is listed in `urls`. 69 The jar is the source of truth afterwards: if the website rotates or refreshes cookies (via `Set-Cookie`, including on redirects, or js executed on the page), the updated cookies are used for all subsequent requests. 70 To keep rotated cookies consistent, pages are rendered one at a time and never while other requests are in flight, regardless of `requestConcurrency` (see the `exclusiveRendering` option to disable this). 71 72 ```javascript 73 await scrape({ 74 urls: ['https://example.com/'], 75 directory: '/path/to/save', 76 request: { 77 headers: { Cookie: 'session=abc123' } 78 }, 79 plugins: [ new PuppeteerPlugin() ] 80 }); 81 ``` 82 83 ## How it works 84 It starts Chromium in headless mode which just opens page and waits until page is loaded. 85 It is far from ideal because probably you need to wait until some resource is loaded or click some button or log in. Currently this module doesn't support such functionality. 86

If you'd like to sponsor this project and have your avatar or company logo appear below [click here](https://github.com/sponsors/s0ph1e). 💖 ## Requirements * nodejs version >= 20 * website-scraper version >= 6 ## Installation ```sh npm install website-scraper website-scraper-puppeteer ``` ### Installing Chrome Puppeteer normally downloads a compatible version of Chrome automatically during installation via a `postinstall` script. Starting with **npm v12**, lifecycle scripts (including `postinstall`) are disabled by default, so this automatic download no longer runs. You may then see an error like `Could not find Chrome (ver. ...)` when scraping. If you use **npm v12 or newer** (or another package manager that blocks install scripts, e.g. recent `pnpm`), install Chrome manually after installing the packages: ```sh npx puppeteer browsers install chrome ``` Alternatives: * Re-enable install scripts by adding `puppeteer` to the [`allowScripts`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#allow-scripts) field in your `package.json` (or `.npmrc`), so the browser is downloaded automatically again. * Use a Chrome/Chromium already installed on your system by pointing Puppeteer to it via `launchOptions.executablePath` (or the `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` environment variable). See Puppeteer's guide on [why automatic downloads can be blocked](https://pptr.dev/guides/installation#automatic-downloads-can-be-blocked) for more details. ## Usage ```javascript import scrape from 'website-scraper'; import PuppeteerPlugin from 'website-scraper-puppeteer'; await scrape({ urls: ['https://www.instagram.com/gopro/'], directory: '/path/to/save', plugins: [ new PuppeteerPlugin({ launchOptions: { headless: true }, /* optional */ gotoOptions: { waitUntil: "networkidle0" }, /* optional */ scrollToBottom: { timeout: 10000, viewportN: 10 }, /* optional */ exclusiveRendering: true, /* optional */ }) ] }); ``` Puppeteer plugin constructor accepts the following params: * `launchOptions` - *(optional)* - puppeteer launch options, can be found in [puppeteer docs](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.launchoptions) * `gotoOptions` - *(optional)* - puppeteer page.goto options, can be found in [puppeteer docs](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.gotooptions) * `scrollToBottom` - *(optional)* - in some cases, the page needs to be scrolled down to render its assets (lazyloading). Because some pages can be really endless, the scrolldown process can be interrupted before reaching the bottom when one or both of the limitations below are reached: * `timeout` - in milliseconds * `viewportN` - viewport height multiplier * `exclusiveRendering` - *(optional, default `true`)* - render pages one at a time and never while other requests are in flight, so cookies rotated by a page (see [Cookies](#cookies)) are never presented stale. Set to `false` for websites which don't rotate cookies: pages are then rendered concurrently, which is considerably faster on large websites. ## Cookies Cookies passed in `request.headers.Cookie` (website-scraper option) are set into the browser's cookie jar for the scraped urls' hosts (including their subdomains), so pages opened in puppeteer send them too — but they are not leaked to other domains. This also applies when a scraped url redirects to a different host (e.g. `example.com` → `shop.example.net`): the redirect target does not receive the configured cookies unless its host is listed in `urls`. The jar is the source of truth afterwards: if the website rotates or refreshes cookies (via `Set-Cookie`, including on redirects, or js executed on the page), the updated cookies are used for all subsequent requests. To keep rotated cookies consistent, pages are rendered one at a time and never while other requests are in flight, regardless of `requestConcurrency` (see the `exclusiveRendering` option to disable this). ```javascript await scrape({ urls: ['https://example.com/'], directory: '/path/to/save', request: { headers: { Cookie: 'session=abc123' } }, plugins: [ new PuppeteerPlugin() ] }); ``` ## How it works It starts Chromium in headless mode which just opens page and waits until page is loaded. It is far from ideal because probably you need to wait until some resource is loaded or click some button or log in. Currently this module doesn't support such functionality.

After evaluating the testability requirements and existing rendering serialization logic, I've confirmed that the cleanest implementation solution is to integrate the attachPage logic into the RequestRenderLock class as an instance method, with per-instance pending request state storage. This design is fully compatible with both exclusive and non-exclusive rendering scenarios.

I've worked out a targeted fix: I'll adjust the finally logic in renderPage so that detach only removes listeners and disables interception, without clearing pending requests. Only request completion events will trigger pending request clearing. This way, tests can accurately verify if there are pending request leaks after a failed goto.

I've identified a potential race condition risk: when page.close() is called with in-flight requests, Target closed errors may trigger requestfailed events, and if the detach operation runs before these events, pending residues will appear, causing dirty states in the next render. content.thinking:
Confirmed: a request that was continued but gets no server response produces NO terminal event on either page.close() or setRequestInterception(false). 

It has been found that request/requestfinished/requestfailed event tracking can’t handle such unresponsive requests. Puppeteer’s networkidle tracking uses frame lifecycle events instead of raw request counting. Three candidate solutions have been worked out, and it has been confirmed that the pending counter is designed to prevent networkidle wait timeouts, so it only needs to account for aborted requests triggered by the requestfailed event.

Puppeteer's built-in networkidle tracking already properly handles aborted requests via the requestfailed event, so our counter is purely an observability and safety feature. I've confirmed there's no extra network hang risk from our interception logic, and the timeout test will pass vacuously with this design.

I’ve found the existing weakens the test, so I’ve settled on a revised solution: count all intercepted requests, reset the pending counter to 0 during page teardown, and only run residue checks before teardown in the render phase.

I’ve finalized the implementation plan: track all intercepted requests, zero the pending counter during page teardown, and assert no residue before teardown in tests. All three required tests will pass with this design.

I’ve verified that listening to the requestfailed event is essential to catch the original bug, as unhandled aborted requests would mask the issue otherwise. The pending counter only needs to account for logged requests, and no extra state information is required for the reconciliation.

I’ve found that the original plan to assert no pending requests before teardown conflicts with the actual behavior of no-response subresources, which breaks normal test flows, so this approach is fundamentally incompatible with real scenarios.

I’ve finalized the adjusted design: the pending counter tracks requests across all lifecycle events, explicitly reconciles leftover entries on page teardown, and retains the assertDrained utility for unit tests. Blocking tests will also include checks to verify all requests have proper terminal events.

I’ve confirmed the timeout and redirect/fav scenarios work well with the current design. I’ll adjust the naming, keep the drainAbandoned method and assertDrained utility, update relevant unit tests, and call drainAbandoned in the renderPage close logic.

Starting with **npm v12**, lifecycle scripts (including `postinstall`) are disabled by default, so this automatic download no longer runs. You may then see an error like `Could not find Chrome (ver. ...)` when scraping. If you use **npm v12 or newer** (or another package manager that blocks install scripts, e.g. recent `pnpm`), install Chrome manually after installing the packages: ```sh npx puppeteer browsers install chrome ``` Alternatives: * Re-enable install scripts by adding `puppeteer` to the [`allowScripts`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#allow-scripts) field in your `package.json` (or `.npmrc`), so the browser is downloaded automatically again. * Use a Chrome/Chromium already installed on your system by pointing Puppeteer to it via `launchOptions.executablePath` (or the `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` environment variable). See Puppeteer's guide on [why automatic downloads can be blocked](https://pptr.dev/guides/installation#automatic-downloads-can-be-blocked) for more details. ## Usage ```javascript import scrape from 'website-scraper'; import PuppeteerPlugin from 'website-scraper-puppeteer'; await scrape({ urls: ['https://www.instagram.com/gopro/'], directory: '/path/to/save', plugins: [ new PuppeteerPlugin({ launchOptions: { headless: true }, /* optional */ gotoOptions: { waitUntil: "networkidle0" }, /* optional */ scrollToBottom: { timeout: 10000, viewportN: 10 }, /* optional */ exclusiveRendering: true, /* optional */ }) ] }); ``` Puppeteer plugin constructor accepts the following params: * `launchOptions` - *(optional)* - puppeteer launch options, can be found in [puppeteer docs](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.launchoptions) * `gotoOptions` - *(optional)* - puppeteer page.goto options, can be found in [puppeteer docs](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.gotooptions) * `scrollToBottom` - *(optional)* - in some cases, the page needs to be scrolled down to render its assets (lazyloading). Because some pages can be really endless, the scrolldown process can be interrupted before reaching the bottom when one or both of the limitations below are reached: * `timeout` - in milliseconds * `viewportN` - viewport height multiplier * `exclusiveRendering` - *(optional, default `true`)* - render pages one at a time and never while other requests are in flight, so cookies rotated by a page (see [Cookies](#cookies)) are never presented stale. Set to `false` for websites which don't rotate cookies: pages are then rendered concurrently, which is considerably faster on large websites. ## Cookies Cookies passed in `request.headers.Cookie` (website-scraper option) are set into the browser's cookie jar for the scraped urls' hosts (including their subdomains), so pages opened in puppeteer send them too — but they are not leaked to other domains. This also applies when a scraped url redirects to a different host (e.g. `example.com` → `shop.example.net`): the redirect target does not receive the configured cookies unless its host is listed in `urls`. The jar is the source of truth afterwards: if the website rotates or refreshes cookies (via `Set-Cookie`, including on redirects, or js executed on the page), the updated cookies are used for all subsequent requests. To keep rotated cookies consistent, pages are rendered one at a time and never while other requests are in flight, regardless of `requestConcurrency` (see the `exclusiveRendering` option to disable this). ```javascript await scrape({ urls: ['https://example.com/'], directory: '/path/to/save', request: { headers: { Cookie: 'session=abc123' } }, plugins: [ new PuppeteerPlugin() ] }); ``` ## How it works It starts Chromium in headless mode which just opens page and waits until page is loaded. It is far from ideal because probably you need to wait until some resource is loaded or click some button or log in. Currently this module doesn't support such functionality.

content.text:
完成。下面是改动总结。

## 实现要点

**新增插件参数（`lib/index.js` 构造函数）**，不传时行为与原来完全一致：
- `blockResourceTypes: []` — 命中类型 abort，其余 continue；含 `document` 或无法识别的类型名直接抛带合法取值列表的 `TypeError`（`document` 有独立错误信息，因为拦截它会白屏）
- `waitUntil` — 限定 `load` / `domcontentloaded` / `networkidle0` / `networkidle2`（也支持数组），对 `gotoOptions.waitUntil` 同样校验
- `timeout` — 非负数，`0` 原样透传表示不超时；非法值抛 `TypeError`
- 两个新参数与 `gotoOptions` 合并时新参数优先，`gotoOptions` 其余字段原样透传，老调用方零改动。校验逻辑放在新文件 `lib/options.js`

**与 render lock 的协同（`lib/requestRenderLock.js`）**：
- 没有第二套监听——`attachInterception` 是页面唯一的 request handler，同一个 request 在同一个回调里只落一个结局，不会触发 `Request is already handled`；`exclusiveRendering: false` 也走同一套
- pending 计数对每个拦截请求 ++，并同时挂 `requestfinished` **和** `requestfailed` 释放（abort 走 failed 分支），所以 abort 不会让 networkidle 类等待挂死
- 实测发现一个边界：被 continue 但服务器永不响应的请求（如无响应的 favicon），`page.close()` 和关闭拦截都**不产生任何终态事件**。detach 在 `page.close()` 之后用 `drainAbandoned()` 把页面销毁作为这类请求的终态 reconcile 掉，计数最终必为 0；超时的 document 则确认由 close 补发的 `requestfailed` 释放（测试断言 `abandoned === 0`，两条路径有区分度）

**测试（`test/puppeteer-plugin.test.js`，共 61 passing）**：
- 新增 fixture `test/mock/blocked-resources.html` + 本地 img/stylesheet/script，file:// 加载：断言 image/stylesheet 被 abort、document/script 正常 continue 且脚本确实执行；另测 networkidle0 在有 abort 时正常 settle
- 慢 document 服务器（请求放行但响应永久 hold）+ 100ms timeout：断言 reject 出干净的 `TimeoutError`、pending 归零无残留
- 拦截器纯单元测试（假 request）覆盖 document 守卫、failed/finished 双分支、assertDrained、abandoned reconcile、abort/continue reject 容错；以及 8 个构造参数校验用例

**验证结果**：
- `npm test`：61 passing，`options.js` 和 `requestRenderLock.js` 覆盖率 100%
- `npx eslint lib test`：我新增/修改的代码**零新增规则问题**。剩余报错分两类，均为基线既有——1331 个 `linebreak-style`（该快照整个仓库以 CRLF 入库，所有文件包括未改动文件都报）；测试文件里 3 个 semi + 1 个 func-names warning 在 HEAD 上就存在（行号因插入而后移）。我给浏览器 fixture 加了 `test/mock/.eslintrc.yml`（沿用 `lib/browserUtils` 的 browser env 先例）

另外新增 `.mocharc.yml` 把 `test/mock/**` 排除出 mocha 递归加载，否则新 fixture 里的 `script.js` 会被当成测试文件执行。README 也补了三个新参数的说明。
